name: Dumbbell Romanian deadlift
instructions: Stand side-on to the camera with your whole body in frame, a dumbbell in each hand. Keep your knees softly bent and push your hips back, lowering the weights along your legs, then drive the hips forward to stand up.

cues.message: Push the hips back further — the hinge is stopping early
Your knees are bending through the lift — this is turning into a squat

knownLimitations: EXPERIMENTAL: no physical validation has been performed. Thresholds are engineering guesses, not measured values.
Hinge depth is torso inclination from vertical, which conflates a hip hinge with rounding at the spine. Spinal position is deliberately not measured and no claim is made about it.
Knee travel is measured against the knee angle captured when the repetition begins, so a set started with already-bent knees calibrates to that starting position.
In a true side view the far-side landmarks are estimated, not observed. The confidence floor is set lower here than for front-view exercises and that is a deliberate accuracy trade.
unsupportedViews: FRONT: a hip hinge is almost entirely along the camera axis and is close to invisible.
FRONT_DIAGONAL: partially visible but torso inclination is foreshortened by an unknown factor; not supported until a validated correction exists.
